clue.text: Award-winning writer's empty Orwellian drama about judge

indicators.note: empty asks for each of the following four words with its insides scooped out, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A prize novelist is described as writing a hollow, dystopian play about a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' applies to all four words, not just Orwellian: ON, DA, AT and JE join up. Michael Ondaatje won the Booker Prize for The English Patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Michael Ondaatje is a Booker Prize-winning novelist and poet.

clue.text: Bars cross, but become warped over time

indicators.note: become warped means the letters twist into a new order

explanation.surface: Crossbars bend out of shape as years pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar is to block or obstruct.

clue.text: Risky and disheartening thing, penning new drama

parts.note: risky means dangerous

indicators.note: penning means enclosing like a pen

parts.note: an apple corer removes the core, the heart, of fruit

explanation.surface: Someone writes a new play about something perilous and depressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartening' suggests depressing; literally it takes the heart out: a CORER. Dangerous Corner is a J. B. Priestley play.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangerous Corner is a 1932 stage play by J. B. Priestley.

clue.text: Female alternative to polo: people kicking bottle about

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: AA, Alcoholics Anonymous, helps people give up drink
a V-neck is an alternative to a polo neck

explanation.surface: A woman chooses something other than polo while people kick a bottle around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'polo' and 'kicking' suggest sport; polo is a jumper neck, and kicking the bottle is quitting drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Ava is a girl's name, as in the actress Ava Gardner.

clue.text: Before he could be said to be quick

definitions.text: Before he could be said to be quick

parts.words: Before he could be said to be quick
parts.note: plays on the idiom for doing something instantly, before you could say a certain man's name

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase before you could say Jack Robinson means very quickly.

clue.text: Sound half of house that Jacques built?

indicators.note: half of says the clue's wall-building phrase supplies just one half of the answer, so the letters appear twice

parts.note: Jacques is a Frenchman, and what he builds as part of a house is a wall, French mur

explanation.surface: A whimsical French twist on the nursery rhyme about the house that Jack built.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'This is the house that Jack built' is turned French: Jacques builds a mur (wall), and the answer is two of those.
explanation.definitionFit: A murmur is a low, indistinct noise.

clue.text: Broadminded bloke — such an eccentric

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tolerant man is described as quite the oddball.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone broadminded is hard to shock or offend.

clue.text: Type of horse accompanying general for part of march

parts.note: Field Marshal Montgomery was a famous British general
the shire is a heavy draught horse

explanation.surface: A horse accompanies a general on a military march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'march' looks like soldiers marching; the Welsh Marches are the England-Wales border region, where Montgomeryshire is a historic Welsh county.
explanation.definitionFit: Montgomeryshire is a historic county in the Welsh Marches borderland.

clue.text: Navy welcoming seaman with one ready bow

indicators.note: welcoming means taking the following letters inside

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
OS is an ordinary seaman
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The navy welcomes a sailor holding a bow ready for action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' suggests a ship's front or archery; it is a violin bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosin is resin rubbed on to prepare a violin bow so it grips the strings.

clue.text: Outlaw sent to bed clutching ball and badge

indicators.note: clutching means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a ship sunk has been sent to the sea bed
a ball is a formal dance
an ID badge identifies the wearer

explanation.surface: A bandit is packed off to bed holding a ball and a badge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent to bed' suggests sleep, but here it is the sea bed: SUNK. The Sundance Kid was an American Wild West outlaw, partner of Butch Cassidy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sundance Kid was a notorious Wild West bandit.

clue.text: Are these positions, set areas, an asset?

indicators.note: set here means lodged inside, so the answer sits within the following run of words

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether particular placements of zones would be advantageous.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through 'areAS AN ASset'. Asanas are yoga postures.
explanation.definitionFit: Asanas are the postures held in yoga practice.

clue.text: Meteoric bursts straddling extremely short interval

indicators.note: straddling means sitting astride, enclosing the next piece
bursts means the word breaks apart and reforms

parts.note: extremely means very

explanation.surface: Meteor showers spread across a brief gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursts' looks like a noun describing meteors; it is the anagram signal. The scrambled METEORIC (RECOTIME) splits so that its letters straddle the word for extremely.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovery time is the brief rest needed to get back to normal after effort.

clue.text: Discharge chap in strange attire

indicators.note: in places the chap inside the other piece, as if wearing it

parts.note: rum is an old British word for strange; the chap is dressed in it
a chap is a male, he

explanation.surface: A man wears odd clothing and is ejected.
explanation.walkthrough: RUM is old-fashioned British slang for odd. The chap HE is pictured dressed in the strange garb.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Have the other Europeans support Force with cheer

indicators.note: support in a down clue puts the Europeans underneath

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them
a whoop is a shout of joy
E is European, twice

explanation.surface: Europeans back a military force with cheering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the other' is British slang for sex; to make whoopee means to have it.
explanation.definitionFit: Make whoopee is a coy euphemism for having sex, which 'the other' also denotes.

clue.text: On horse, rode back bringing musical instrument

parts.note: re means on or about, as in business letters

indicators.note: back turns both horse and rode around together

parts.note: a nag is an old horse

explanation.surface: Someone rides a horse back home bringing an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the horse and 'rode' as a single run (EDORGAN), not just the nearest word.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed organ is a keyboard instrument sounding through vibrating reeds, like a harmonium.

clue.text: Having cold joint and jam sandwich sailor's full!

indicators.note: sandwich means the outer pieces enclose the sailor between them

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
the hock is a leg joint, as in ham hock
to jam or lock is to stick fast
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor with cold meat and a jam sandwich declares himself stuffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jam sandwich' looks like food; jam is LOCK, and the joint and jam together sandwich the AB.
explanation.definitionFit: Chock-a-block means crammed full, a nautical term for tackle hauled tight.

clue.text: Pack case for Montego Bay, having a year off

indicators.note: off means these letters are dropped from the nickname

parts.note: MoBay is the local nickname for Montego Bay in Jamaica

explanation.surface: Packing a suitcase for a holiday in Jamaica after a year away.
explanation.walkthrough: Montego Bay, Jamaica, is known locally as MoBay; take off A and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A mob is a crowd or pack of people or animals.

clue.text: My overwhelming love for pop star

indicators.note: overwhelming means engulfing the next letter

parts.note: my and by George are both exclamations of surprise
love is zero, O, in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about their enormous love for a pop singer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is the exclamation, like 'By George!'. Boy George was the singer of Culture Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Boy George is the 1980s singer who fronted Culture Club.

clue.text: Girl related tips on ingenious origami process

indicators.note: tips on asks for the far end letters of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A girl passes on handy hints about paper folding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice; it is the letters at the ends of the three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister is a girl related to you by having the same parents.

clue.text: Shrub with place in the ground — and a second being talked of

parts.note: to inter is to place in a grave

indicators.note: being talked of signals a word heard rather than read

parts.note: a second way to place in the ground is to bury

explanation.surface: A shrub is planted, then a second one is discussed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a second' means a second word for 'place in the ground': BURY, which sounds like BERRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Winterberry is a deciduous holly bush with red fruit lasting through winter.

clue.text: Quietly passionate old officer — ultimately sexy but not original

parts.note: P is piano, quietly in music
hot means passionate
a cop is a police officer

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of sexy

explanation.surface: A description of a quietly ardent former officer who is attractive but unoriginal.
explanation.definitionFit: A photocopy is a duplicate, not the original document.

clue.text: Particular image you know initially must arise

parts.note: pic is short for picture

indicators.note: arise in a down clue means reading upwards
initially takes the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A specific picture, you know, must come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Being particular means being fussy and choosy.

clue.text: There's to be a sequel and series in Return of Amadeus, next

definitions.text: There's to be a sequel and series

indicators.note: Return of says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, across the word break

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Talk of a follow-up film series to Amadeus.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked the hiding signal: 'in' marks the hidden run amadEUS NExt, and 'Return of' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow on as a consequence, as a sequel or series does.

clue.text: Party food has potential to take off

parts.note: can means is able to
to ape is to mimic or take off

explanation.surface: A snack at a party looks likely to become popular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' suggests success; it means imitate.
explanation.definitionFit: A canape is a small savoury snack served at drinks parties.

clue.text: Doctor is like comforter when failing body less healthy

indicators.note: doctor means tamper with, so these letters are rearranged
failing body means the word loses all but its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A physician resembles a comforter when someone's body gives out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb, not a medic. Comforter with its body gone is CR; shuffle with ISLIKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sicklier is the comparative of sickly, meaning more unwell.

clue.text: See 9
Woman, head in state after her son's delivery

indicators.note: after places the woman's letters following the son's

parts.note: the Queen's son Andrew held the title Duke of York
ER is Elizabeth Regina, a woman who was head of state

explanation.surface: A woman leading a state comes after her son's childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her' refers back to the Queen (ER), whose son Prince Andrew was Duke of York. A YORKER is a cricket ball pitched right at the batsman's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler's delivery aimed at the batsman's toes is a yorker.

clue.text: After "live" commercial's repeated you alert viewer

indicators.note: After places the commercial following the word for live

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
an ad is a commercial

indicators.note: repeated means the word for you appears twice

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: After a live broadcast, adverts keep you watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A beady eye is a watchful, sharp gaze.
